# Test fixtures

Every file in this directory plus its provenance. All fixtures are project-owned and either hand-authored or generated by a committed script.

## Image fixtures

### `hello.png`

- **What**: 400×100 PNG with the text "Hello World" on a white background.
- **Why**: The canonical positive OCR fixture. Also embedded inside `document-photo.png`.

### `empty.png`

- **What**: 200×100 blank white PNG.
- **Why**: Negative OCR fixture — Vision returns no observations for an image with no text.

### `document-photo.png`

- **What**: 600×800 PNG that looks like a photo of a printed document on a gray surface, containing a perspective-distorted copy of `hello.png`.
- **Why**: A more realistic OCR/searchable-PDF input than the flat `hello.png`; still recognizes "Hello World".
- **Generator**: `scripts/generate-document-fixtures.swift` (deterministic — fixed stripe widths and perspective coordinates).

## PDF fixtures

### `multipage.pdf`

- **What**: 3-page vector PDF with "Page One", "Page Two", "Page Three".
- **Why**: Canonical multi-page fixture — exercises lazy page rendering, per-page streaming, the `page`/`pageCount` envelope fields, and vector-safe `searchable-pdf` output.

### `scanned-200dpi.pdf`

- **What**: Single-page PDF embedding a 400×100 image into a 144×36-point page (≈200 DPI).
- **Why**: Regression fixture for `--pdf-dpi auto` — the detector should render at ~200 DPI, not the 144 fallback.

### `scanned-form-xobject.pdf`

- **What**: PDF whose page image is wrapped in a Form XObject (a common Acrobat-OCR pattern).
- **Why**: `--pdf-dpi auto` must recurse into Form XObjects to find the underlying Image XObject.

### `huge-mediabox.pdf`

- **What**: PDF with a 6000×6000-point MediaBox (625 MP at 300 DPI).
- **Why**: Regression fixture for the 200 MP render cap — `--pdf-dpi 300` should throw a clean "megapixel" error rather than OOM.

### `encrypted.pdf`

- **What**: Single-page vector PDF reading "Hello World", encrypted with user+owner password `secret`.
- **Why**: Used by the Node end-to-end test for encrypted-PDF handling. It covers the main-thread `ocr()` path through the real binary; a shim test covers one-shot environment forwarding. The Swift suite generates encrypted PDFs at runtime, so this fixture is only needed for Node tests.
- **Generator**: `scripts/generate-document-fixtures.swift`. Content-deterministic only: PDF encryption embeds random salts, so regenerated bytes always differ. Tests assert on behavior, never fixture bytes.

## Non-image fixtures

### `invalid.txt`

- **What**: Plain text ("not image data").
- **Why**: Asserts a clean "Cannot read image" error on non-image input rather than a crash.

### `words.txt`

- **What**: One custom-vocabulary word per line.
- **Why**: Regression fixture for `--custom-words-file`.

## When to commit a new fixture

A new fixture belongs here when it is either (1) deterministically reproducible via a committed generator script, or (2) has explicit provenance and a redistribution-friendly license. Add a section to this README before the fixture lands.
